About the Umm al-Qura calendar

The Umm al-Qura calendar is Saudi Arabia's official Hijri calendar. It is calculated astronomically, so month starts are known in advance, and government transactions, residence permits and contracts rely on it. The start of Ramadan, Shawwal and Dhu al-Hijjah is announced by moon sighting, so it can differ from the calendar by a day, and between countries. The calculator uses the "islamic-umalqura" calendar built into your browser, which covers the years 1300 to 1600 AH.

To convert any date between the two calendars use the Hijri–Gregorian date converter; for your age in Hijri years, the Hijri age calculator; and for the gap between two dates, the days between dates calculator.

Frequently asked questions

What is today's Hijri date?

It appears at the top of this page, worked out from your device's date by the Umm al-Qura calendar used officially in Saudi Arabia, with the weekday and the Gregorian date. Countries that start months by moon sighting may differ by a day.

When does the Hijri year 1449 begin?

1 Muharram 1449 falls on Sunday 6 June 2027 by the Umm al-Qura calendar; the year 1448 began on Tuesday 16 June 2026.

How many days are in the Hijri year 1448?

355 days by the Umm al-Qura calendar, with seven months of 30 days and five of 29. The year 1449 has 354 days.

What is the difference between the Umm al-Qura calendar and moon sighting?

The Umm al-Qura calendar is calculated astronomically and used for official transactions in Saudi Arabia, while the start of Ramadan and the Eids is announced by moon sighting, which can differ from the calendar by a day.
